mappings.note: Asks the learner to name India's major landforms (C-SST1.1, identify and describe landforms) and then justify them by water supply and climate, which is the geography-to-life link of C-SST1.2-LO-2. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, because nothing about how the Himalayas or the plateau were formed is required.

A counterfactual about cold Central Asian winds, monsoon and river flow if the Himalayas were absent - purely the interrelationship between climate and the life of people. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, which would require the mechanism of the range's formation.

The 'mini-continent' answer is an inventory of landforms - mountains, plains, desert, plateau, coasts - so it sits on the identify-and-describe-landforms competency. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, since no map or globe work and no climatic-region boundary is asked for.
Tracing a river and listing how people use it at each stage is the human-use side of the frame. Not C-SST1.3-LO-3: the task is to enumerate uses, not to argue for conserving the water.

Requires describing two landform terms, peninsula and plateau, as they apply to southern India. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, because the expected answer is a definition of the present shape, not the process that raised it.
The answer turns on why protecting Himalayan flora and fauna, including the snow leopard, matters - the conservation-sensitivity outcome. Not C-SST1.1, since no landform has to be described.

An explicit map exercise: open the physical and political maps and place yourself against a feature. LO-1 is the only locate-on-a-map outcome in this frame; it is worded for climatic regions, but the skill assessed is map location, so it is the closest honest fit rather than the C-SST1.1 description competency.
Food preservation methods varying with local climate is exactly the climate-to-daily-life link. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1: nothing is being located, the regions are only the backdrop.
Asks how diverse physical and climatic regions still support one shared life, which is the interrelationship outcome. Not CG-SST1, because the more specific LO covers it.

Recall of the five physiographic divisions of India - identifying landform regions. One of a cluster of factual-recall landform items in this chapter that the frame can only serve through this competency, there being no India-physiography LO.

Defines hydroelectricity, i.e. water as an energy resource; the goal is the only code covering the distribution and use of resources. Not C-SST1.3-LO-3, which asks for sensitivity to conserving energy, not a definition of how it is generated.

Reading a physical map's colour legend as altitude is a map-interpretation item, so LO-1 rather than the descriptive C-SST1.1. The distractors are soil, climate zone and population - all map-legend readings.
Recall of the Himalayan range's extent across six countries - a description of the landform. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because the thing being bounded is a mountain range, not a climatic region.
Identifies the glacier that is the source of the Bhagirathi - a landform-identification fact. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2: no formation process is involved, only which glacier it is.
The India-Eurasia collision is the formation mechanism of a landform, so LO-2 rather than the bare C-SST1.1. Distractors are other plate pairings, so the item really tests the causal process.

The Sanskrit gloss 'abode of snow' is a description of the range's defining character, which the identify-and-describe competency covers. No LO fits a vocabulary item, and C-SST1.2-LO-1 would be wrong since nothing is located.

The discriminator between Himadri and Himachal in the key is habitability - year-round snow versus a climate that supports settlement - so the climate-and-life outcome. Not C-SST1.1, because every distractor that is only about relief or forest cover is wrong.

Kath-kuni and dhajji-dewari building in stone and wood is an adaptation of housing to a cold, seismic mountain setting. Not C-SST1.1-LO-1: the materials are building materials, not the rock-type classification that LO-1 means.

Ladakh's 'moonland' relief is explained by folding during the landmass collision - a formation-of-landforms item, and the distractors are rival processes (volcanism, glaciation, wind). Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, though Ladakh is a cold desert, since the climate is not what is asked.
The yak's role in milk, wool, transport and fuel is how high-altitude people live off their environment. Not C-SST1.3-LO-3: the yak is a livelihood animal here, not a conservation subject.

Fertility of the Gangetic Plains traced to mineral-rich sediment laid down by Himalayan rivers - the formation of an alluvial landform. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because the key is the depositional process, not what farmers do with it.

Why a flat plain carries a dense road and rail network is terrain shaping human activity. Not C-SST1.1, because the plain's own description is assumed and the reasoning is about movement of people and goods.

Taanka and kunds are rainwater harvesting - the conservation of water outcome. Chosen over C-SST1.2-LO-2, which would fit the arid-climate adaptation, because the structures exist specifically to save a scarce resource.

The Aravallis checking the Thar's eastward spread is about the extent of an arid region, which is what the locate-climatic-regions outcome addresses. Not C-SST1.1, since the point is the desert's boundary rather than the hills themselves.
Naming the Western and Eastern Ghats as the plateau's flanks is landform identification. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, as no map task or climatic region is involved.

The west-to-east flow of the Deccan rivers follows from the plateau's eastward tilt - a description of the landform's slope. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, because the tilt is given, not explained as a formation process.

Recall of the southern limit of the West Coast - identification of a coastal landform's extent. One of the chapter's factual-recall landform items; no LO in this frame covers Indian physiography more narrowly.

A delta is defined by the depositional process that builds it, so this is formation-of-landforms rather than the bare identification competency. The distractors are other formation processes: glacial, volcanic, erosional.
Matching each island group to its sea is identification of landforms and their setting. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because the pairing is done from memory, not from a map or globe.
Identifies which river systems build the Sundarbans delta - a landform identification. Not C-SST1.3-LO-3, despite the mangroves, since the item never touches conservation.
Placing the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills within the Meghalaya Plateau is landform identification. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1: the plateau is a relief unit and no map reading is required.

The stem gives a climate profile - moderate temperatures, rich biodiversity, hill stations - and asks which Himalayan belt it is, so the learner is placing a climatic region. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because no aspect of how people live has to be explained, only the belt named.

The wrong pairing is Ladakh as a hot desert when it is a cold desert - a climatic-region classification. Not C-SST1.1, because the three correct pairings are all climate or land-character labels, not formation or relief facts.

Recall of where the Great Himalayan National Park lies, i.e. of a flora-and-fauna reserve, which puts it in the conservation lane. Not C-SST1.1, since a national park is a protected area rather than a landform.
Defines 'archipelago' as a landform term using Lakshadweep as the example. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, which would need the coral-building process rather than the definition.

Asks what the Ladakh rocks are made of - sand and clay of marine origin - which is the rock-types part of LO-1. Chosen over C-SST1.1-LO-2 because the composition, not the folding, is what the answer turns on.

The assertion-reason pair tests whether Himalayan snowmelt is what sustains millions downstream - the mountain-to-livelihood link. Not CG-SST1, because the specific LO already carries the water-and-people relationship.

The statement judged correct is that the Himalayas form India's northern natural barrier - a description of a landform's position and role. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because the item stops at the barrier and never reaches its effect on people.

Mineral wealth of the Aravallis - marble, granite, zinc, copper - is the spatial distribution of resources, which only the goal covers. Not C-SST1.1-LO-1: LO-1 means classifying rock types in a diagram, whereas these are named as economic minerals.
